name: ChatGPT
description: OpenAI's general-purpose conversational assistant. It drafts and edits documents, explains concepts, writes and debugs code, analyzes uploaded files, and generates images, with memory and custom instructions that persist across conversations.

name: Claude
description: Anthropic's assistant, built around careful reasoning and large context windows. Particularly strong at long-document analysis, nuanced professional writing, and multi-step tasks executed through tool use and Projects.

name: Gemini
description: Google's multimodal assistant, woven into Search and Workspace. Handles text, images, audio and code in one conversation, and grounds answers in fresh web results when asked.

name: Microsoft Copilot
description: Microsoft's assistant baked into Windows, Edge and Bing. Answers questions with cited web sources, generates images, and on Windows machines can adjust settings and summarize documents.

name: Poe
description: Quora's aggregator for chatting with many frontier and open models under one subscription. Includes a bot builder for combining a base model with your own instructions.

name: Perplexity
description: An answer engine that searches the live web and replies with concise summaries whose every claim is footnoted to a source. Focus mode narrows searches to academic papers, forums or social posts.

name: Jasper
description: A marketing writing platform aimed at content teams. Trains a brand voice on your existing copy, then generates campaigns, blog posts and ads that stay inside that voice, with collaboration and review built in.

name: Copy.ai
description: Started as an ad-copy generator and grew into a go-to-market workflow engine. Chains research, drafting and enrichment steps into playbooks for outbound sales and campaign content.

name: Writesonic
description: An AI writer oriented to search traffic: briefs, drafts and optimizes articles against live SERP data, with built-in fact-checking with citations and bulk generation for agencies.

name: Grammarly
description: A writing checker that lives everywhere you type, flagging grammar, clarity and tone issues in real time. The generative layer rewrites sentences and paragraphs, and enterprise plans enforce shared style guides.

name: QuillBot
description: A paraphrasing toolkit popular with students: rewrites sentences in several registers, summarizes long passages, checks grammar and manages citations.

name: Wordtune
description: A sentence-level rewriting assistant. Select any awkward sentence and it offers casual and formal alternatives that keep your meaning while tightening the phrasing.

name: ProWritingAid
description: A deep-editing suite for long-form writers. Beyond grammar it reports on pacing, repetition, dialogue tags and sticky sentences, working inside Word, Google Docs and its own editor.

name: LanguageTool
description: An open-source proofreader covering thirty-plus languages, with a rephrasing mode and honest self-hosting options for teams that want text to stay on their infrastructure.

name: DeepL Write
description: A writing improver from the DeepL translation team. Reworks sentences for precision and natural flow, with tone selection, and pairs with the company's widely used translator.

name: Rytr
description: A lightweight, inexpensive AI writer built around forty-plus use-case templates, from product descriptions to YouTube intros, with tone controls and a plagiarism checker.

name: Anyword
description: A copywriting tool that scores every generated variant against historical ad performance before you publish it, so marketers can pick versions predicted to convert rather than just read well.

name: HyperWrite
description: An everyday writing companion: autowrite continues your drafts, specialized tools handle emails and blog sections, and a personal model learns your voice over time.

name: Sudowrite
description: A creative-writing studio for novelists. It expands rough beats into prose, offers rewrite modes like 'more intense' or 'simpler', and helps brainstorm character and plot twists without hijacking the author's voice.

name: NovelAI
description: A subscription storytelling sandbox with narrative-tuned language models that keep your prose and characters consistent, plus anime-styled image generation, all without training on your private library.

name: Notion AI
description: AI woven directly into Notion pages and databases: ask questions about your workspace, autofill database properties from page content, and draft or summarize any document where you already work.

name: Mem
description: A note repository organized by an AI instead of folders. Everything you capture is embedded and resurfaced by relevance, and its chat answers questions from your own history.

name: Obsidian
description: A local-first knowledge base of plain Markdown files. Its large plugin ecosystem wires in language models for summarizing, tagging and searching a vault that never leaves your machine.

name: Otter.ai
description: A meeting notetaker that joins calls live, transcribes with speaker labels, and pushes summaries and action items to Slack and your calendar. Supports live chat with the transcript during the meeting.

name: Fireflies.ai
description: A conversation-intelligence recorder for sales and team meetings. It transcribes, scores talk time and sentiment, and syncs notes and highlights to CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot.

name: Fathom
description: A free AI notetaker for video calls that records, transcribes and highlights the moments you flag live, then hands you a summary with action items minutes after the call ends.

name: Rewind
description: A personal memory app that indexes what you've seen, said and typed on your Mac so you can search your own history — including meeting details you forgot to note.

name: Gamma
description: A prompt-to-deck generator: describe a topic and it assembles a structured, restyled presentation that you can publish as an interactive web page or export to PowerPoint.

name: Reclaim.ai
description: A smart calendar assistant that defends focus time, schedules habits and books meetings around priorities, replanning your day automatically when things slip.

name: Motion
description: Part project manager, part calendar. It turns task lists, deadlines and meetings into one continuously re-prioritized daily plan for individuals and small teams.

name: Clockwise
description: A calendar optimizer for teams that swaps meetings around to manufacture uninterrupted focus blocks and resolves scheduling conflicts automatically.

name: Superhuman
description: A premium email client rebuilt around speed, with AI that triages your inbox, drafts replies in your voice and splits important mail from noise across Gmail and Outlook.

name: Shortwave
description: An AI inbox on top of Gmail that summarizes threads into digests, pinpoints action items and lets you search and ask questions about years of mail.

name: SaneBox
description: An email triage layer that trains itself on how you treat senders, moving unimportant mail out of the inbox and summarizing what it parked.

name: Miro AI
description: Generative helpers on the Miro whiteboard: expand sticky notes into clusters, summarize boards, synthesize user stories and generate images inside workshops.

name: Whimsical AI
description: One-click expansion for diagrams: give it a seed idea and it grows mind maps and flowcharts, so planning starts structured instead of blank.

name: Airtable AI
description: AI fields inside Airtable bases that summarize records, classify text, draft replies and translate — turning a no-code database into a lightweight automation layer.

name: Raycast
description: A Mac launcher with built-in AI chat, quick commands and an extension store, so answers, snippets and app control are one hotkey away from anywhere.

name: GitHub Copilot
description: The coding assistant embedded in VS Code, JetBrains and github.com. It completes code inline from comments and context, chats about your repository, and drafts pull-request descriptions.

name: Cursor
description: A code editor built AI-first. Its chat indexes your whole repository, applies multi-file edits from a prompt, and steps through terminal commands, with inline completions as you type.

name: Windsurf
description: An agentic IDE from the Codeium team: a flows-with-you assistant that keeps the entire codebase in context, refactors across files and runs the build to check its own work.

name: Tabnine
description: A code completion hub for enterprises that care about provenance: it trains on permissive code only and can run fully inside your VPC while learning team conventions.

name: Sourcegraph Cody
description: A coding assistant with deep code-search roots. It retrieves the relevant slices of large monorepos to answer architecture questions and generate patches grounded in your real code.

name: Snyk
description: A developer-security platform that continuously scans dependencies, containers and IaC for vulnerabilities, then proposes the fix as a pull request you can review in one click.

name: v0 by Vercel
description: A generative UI tool that turns prompts and screenshots into React and Tailwind components built on shadcn/ui, editable in place and deployable to Vercel straight from the draft.

name: bolt.new
description: A browser workspace from StackBlitz that scaffolds full-stack apps from a prompt, runs Node in a WebContainer, installs packages and deploys, without a local setup.

name: Replit
description: A cloud IDE with an AI agent that builds, runs and debugs projects end to end in hosted workspaces, then ships them on Replit's own hosting with databases included.

name: Warp
description: A terminal rebuilt as a modern app: blocks make output copyable, and the built-in agent explains failed commands, suggests the next one and scripts workflows from natural language.

name: Aider
description: An open-source terminal pair programmer. You chat, it edits files across your repo and commits each change to git with a sensible message — scriptable and editor-agnostic.

name: Qodo
description: A code-integrity assistant that analyzes behavior to generate meaningful test suites, review PRs for edge cases and risks, and explain unfamiliar legacy code.

name: Mintlify
description: Documentation that writes itself: it generates and keeps docs in sync with your codebase, answers user questions from those docs, and hosts a polished reference site.

name: LangChain
description: The de-facto framework for LLM applications: chains, agents, tool calls and retrieval patterns in Python and JavaScript, plus LangSmith for tracing what your agents actually did.

name: LlamaIndex
description: A data framework for retrieval-augmented generation: connectors ingest documents and databases, indices chunk and embed them, and query engines answer with citations.

name: Hugging Face
description: The hub of the open-model ecosystem: hundreds of thousands of models and datasets, the transformers library, and hosted inference endpoints for running any of them in production.

name: Hex
description: A collaborative data notebook with an AI copilot that writes and fixes SQL and Python, explains results, and turns cells into shareable interactive apps for stakeholders.

name: Julius AI
description: A conversational analyst: upload a spreadsheet and ask questions in plain English to get charts, regressions and forecasts, with the code it ran shown alongside.

name: Rows
description: A spreadsheet with superpowers aimed at growth and finance teams: live integrations pull data from ads platforms and CRMs, and AI functions analyze it in place.

name: Text2SQL.ai
description: Converts natural-language questions into SQL for your schema, with dialect awareness for Postgres, BigQuery, Snowflake and friends, plus training on your own tables.

name: Polymer
description: A no-code dashboard builder: point it at a spreadsheet and it suggests visualizations and insights, then publishes an interactive dashboard anyone on the team can explore.

name: Metabase
description: An open-source BI tool where anyone can ask questions of company data through a friendly builder or SQL, then save answers as dashboards the whole team can watch.

name: Whisper API
description: OpenAI's speech recognition endpoint: accurate multilingual transcription with translation built in, priced per minute, and fine-tunable on domain vocabulary.

name: ElevenLabs
description: The reference for realistic synthetic speech: instant voices in dozens of languages, cloning from minutes of audio, and dubbing that preserves the original speaker's tone.

name: Murf AI
description: A voiceover studio with a hundred-plus studio voices: control pitch, pauses and emphasis per word, sync to slides or video, and iterate without re-booking talent.

name: Descript
description: Edits audio and video by editing the transcript: delete a sentence and the media follows. Studio Sound cleans recordings, and overdub fixes flubs in a cloned voice.

name: Runway
description: A generative video toolkit used in real film production: text-to-video, image-to-video with camera control, inpainting and frame interpolation, organized around a timeline editor.

name: Pika
description: A playful text-to-video studio: animate ideas with camera moves and effects, remix product shots and memes, and publish vertical clips straight to social.

name: Luma Dream Machine
description: Photorealistic video generation from text or images with physically coherent motion, from the team behind leading neural capture research.

name: Synthesia
description: Studio-quality avatar videos from a script: pick a presenter or clone yourself, type the narration, and get the same video re-voiced in 130+ languages for training libraries.

name: HeyGen
description: Photorealistic avatars and video translation with lip-sync: turn one recording into dozens of localized versions, or generate personalized outreach at scale.

name: Opus Clip
description: Chops long videos and podcasts into short vertical clips: it finds the hooks, reframes to keep faces centered, adds captions and scores virality.

name: VEED
description: A browser video editor with AI conveniences: auto-subtitles in many languages, eye-contact correction, noise removal and text-to-speech voiceovers.

name: Kapwing
description: A collaborative web editor for teams making social content: smart cut removes silences, resizing reflows for every platform, and teammates comment right on the timeline.

name: Suno
description: Turns a text prompt into a finished song — lyrics, vocals and arrangement across genres — and lets you extend or remix your own stems.

name: AIVA
description: An AI composer focused on orchestral and cinematic scoring: generate full tracks in a style profile, then edit the MIDI piano roll like any DAW.

name: Mubert
description: Generates endless royalty-free soundtracks per mood and activity, usable in content, apps and streams via API, with clear commercial licensing.

name: Krisp
description: A call enhancer that removes background noise and echo from your microphone in any conferencing app, layering live transcription and meeting notes on top.

name: AssemblyAI
description: A speech-intelligence API beyond transcription: chapters, topics, sentiment, auto-chapters and PII redaction over audio streams or files.

name: Deepgram
description: Fast, accurate speech recognition built on its own foundation models, with streaming and batch APIs, diarization and on-prem deployment.

name: Wondercraft
description: A text-to-podcast studio: pick realistic AI hosts, add music beds, and regenerate whole episodes in another language from the same script.

name: Midjourney
description: The image model with the strongest aesthetic signature: painterly, cinematic renders steered by text and reference images, edited in a web canvas with region-aware tools.

name: DALL·E 3
description: OpenAI's image generator, known for following elaborate prompts closely and rendering legible text. Available through ChatGPT and a developer API with inpainting.

name: Stable Diffusion
description: Stability AI's open-weight image family. Self-hostable and endlessly fine-tunable, with the largest ecosystem of community checkpoints, LoRAs and ControlNets.

name: FLUX
description: Black Forest Labs' diffusion-transformer family with excellent prompt adherence and text rendering, available both as open weights for local use and via API.

name: Ideogram
description: The text-to-image model to pick when the image must contain readable words: posters, logos and layouts come out with clean typography instead of alphabet soup.

name: Leonardo.Ai
description: A production image platform for game and product teams: fine-tuned style models, a canvas editor with inpainting, and consistent characters across generations.

name: Krea
description: A real-time generation canvas: sketch or move objects and the render updates instantly, with upscalers and style training in the same workspace.

name: Playground
description: A browser design editor where generation meets layout: templates, editing and image models together for marketing graphics rather than pure art.

name: Remove.bg
description: Does one thing perfectly: strips backgrounds from photos with pixel-precise edges — hair included — via web, desktop apps and an API used by e-commerce pipelines.

name: Photoroom
description: Turns phone photos into studio product shots: cut out the item, drop in realistic backgrounds and shadows, batch-process a whole catalog from the mobile app.

name: Magnific
description: An AI upscaler that hallucinates convincing detail: feed a low-resolution render and get a gallery-grade enlargement with adjustable creativity.

name: Picsart
description: A creative ecosystem on mobile and web: AI background removal, object cleanup, style filters and quick logo makers, plus a stock library.

name: Craiyon
description: The free, lightweight generator descended from DALL·E mini. Perfect for quick concept sketches and memes; not pretending to be production art.

name: NightCafe
description: An aggregator studio hosting multiple open models, daily art challenges and a big community gallery — a social layer on top of generation.

name: Lexica
description: A search engine for Stable Diffusion art with the prompts attached — browse millions of images, lift the prompt that made the look, then generate your own.

name: Clipdrop
description: A toolbox of focused photo utilities — cleanup, relight, uncrop, upscale, swap — each available as a one-click app and a clean API.

name: Adobe Firefly
description: Adobe's commercially-safe generative models, embedded across Photoshop, Illustrator and Express — generative fill and expand on real layered documents.

name: Canva Magic Studio
description: The AI layer across Canva: Magic Write drafts copy, Magic Design assembles on-brand layouts from a prompt, and background tools clean up photos inside templates.

name: Figma AI
description: AI inside the industry's design tool: generate first-draft layouts from a prompt, auto-rename layers, replace placeholder content, and turn selections into prototypes.

name: Uizard
description: Turns hand-drawn sketches and plain-English prompts into editable multi-platform app designs, wireframes first and pixel-perfect later.

name: Galileo AI
description: Text-prompt to high-fidelity UI: full app screens with consistent components, exportable to Figma for the design team to refine.

name: Looka
description: A logo maker that finishes the job: generate marks from a brief, then export a complete brand kit — colors, fonts, business cards and social profiles.

name: Beautiful.ai
description: Presentations that arrange themselves: add content and the slide re-lays-out to stay on brand, so teams stop nudging text boxes.

name: Tome
description: A narrative deck generator for sales and storytelling: a prompt becomes a structured presentation with generated imagery, ready to personalize per prospect.

name: Vizcom
description: Sketch-to-render for industrial and concept designers: rough line work becomes shaded, material-rich renders in seconds, preserving your stroke intent.

name: Kittl
description: A design platform with serious typography — ornate display faces, vector generation and mockups aimed at merch and print-on-demand creators.

name: Intercom Fin
description: A support agent that resolves customer conversations from your help center, with answers it can cite, confidence-based handoff to humans, and per-resolution pricing.

name: Ada
description: An enterprise AI customer-service platform resolving inquiries across chat, email and voice in 100+ languages, with guardrails and analytics tuned for regulated industries.

name: Kommunicate
description: A chatbot builder that combines GPT-powered answers grounded in your docs with smooth human handoff and a tidy inbox for the agents.

name: Chatbase
description: Upload documents or point it at your site and it ships a chatbot grounded in that content, embeddable anywhere, with analytics on what customers actually ask.

name: Zapier AI
description: AI woven through 7,000+ app integrations: build Zaps by describing them, let chatbots answer from connected tools, and add AI steps to any automation.

name: Surfer SEO
description: An on-page SEO editor that scores your draft against the live top results for a keyword and tells you, section by section, what to cover to compete.

name: Frase
description: Compresses the SERP research loop: it reads the top-ranking pages for your query, writes the brief, then helps draft and optimize the article against them.

name: Clearscope
description: Content optimization reports for editorial teams: a letter grade, the terms to cover, and readability — inside Google Docs or its own editor.

name: SE Ranking
description: A full SEO suite with an AI writer on top: track rankings, audit sites and research keywords, then draft search-optimized articles from the tracked clusters.

name: AdCreative.ai
description: Generates ad creatives scored against conversion history before you spend: copy variants, images and video sized per placement, wired to your ad accounts.

name: Apollo.io
description: A B2B sales platform pairing a huge contact database with AI: it prospects lookalike buyers, sequences emails and summarizes calls.

name: Elicit
description: A research assistant over 125 million academic papers: ask a question, get a table of relevant studies with methods and findings extracted into comparable columns.

name: Consensus
description: A search engine for scientific claims: it answers yes/no questions by tallying what peer-reviewed papers say, with each supporting paper one click deep.

name: Semantic Scholar
description: An AI-enhanced literature index from the Allen Institute: influential-citation weighting, TLDR summaries of papers and feeds that learn your niche.

name: Scite
description: Smart citations that classify how a paper was used — supporting, contrasting or merely mentioned — so you see the argument around a claim, not just its count.

name: SciSpace
description: A PDF reader built for papers: explains symbols and jargon in place, answers questions about the document and assembles a literature table across your library.

name: Khanmigo
description: Khan Academy's Socratic tutor: guides K-12 and college students through problems step by step with hints instead of answers, with teacher dashboards alongside.

name: Quizlet
description: The study platform's AI layer turns any material into adaptive flashcards and practice tests, and its tutor walks you through what you keep missing.

name: Duolingo Max
description: The subscription tier of the language app where learners role-play scenarios — ordering coffee, interviewing — with an AI that gently corrects their mistakes in context.

name: Photomath
description: Point your camera at a handwritten equation and get the solution with each step explained, plus interactive graphs for the underlying function.

name: Trello
description: Atlassian's board tool with an AI layer that summarizes cards, drafts checklists and answers 'what's stale on this board?' for team standups.

name: Todoist
description: The classic to-do list with an assistant that decomposes vague goals into scheduled tasks and filters your day down to what actually matters.
